messages:
sam: heads up — ran into a socket/worker stall in the python sample app when cancelling an SSE-style streaming request from inside a queued worker. reproducible on dev machine.

sam: short repro: spawn 10 workers, each hits /generate streaming endpoint, cancel half ~200ms after first chunk. some workers never finish and sockets stay in CLOSE_WAIT.

sam: minimal client generator (py3.10, httpx async):
```python
async def stream_gen(client, url):
    async with client.stream('GET', url) as resp:
        async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes():
            yield chunk
```

sam: cancellation happens via task.cancel() in worker. observed: generator stops yielding, finalization not running, connection not returned to pool.

elaine: ugh. seen something like this with httpx + uvicorn where aclose isn't awaited. did you try wrapping with try/finally and calling await resp.aclose()?

sam: yep tried try/finally in the generator, but finalizer sometimes doesn't run if cancel was raised in the middle of aiter_bytes(). looks like generator exit order / weakref finalizer race.

nick: can you paste the worker loop? maybe we're forgetting to await task cancellation result which keeps socket open.

sam: worker uses asyncio.create_task and waits on gather with return_exceptions. we call t.cancel() then await t. sometimes await t hangs.

matt: quick thought: type of generator currently annotated as AsyncGenerator[bytes, None] in sdk. but our public helper returns AsyncIterator[bytes]. mypy may not catch, but the semantics differ for aclose(). AsyncGenerator has aclose method invoked by await agen.aclose(), but AsyncIterator may not.

elaine: true — SDK surface should guarantee aclose semantics for stream iterators so user code can reliably close. if we return an object with __anext__ but no aclose, cancelling may not flush.

devex-bot: CI report attached: 3 failing tests related to streaming cancel on py-3.11, httpx 0.24 in matrix.

sam: workaround that helped locally: wrap resp.stream in an explicit async context manager in worker, and on CancelledError call await resp.aclose() in except/finally. but it's brittle.

nick: can we change SDK to return a custom AsyncGenerator wrapper that implements __aiter__, __anext__, and an explicit aclose that calls resp.aclose()? then callers can do:
```python
async for chunk in client.stream(...):
    ...
# and on cancel we ensure await stream.aclose() in finally
```

matt: sounds reasonable. also need to update typing to expose AsyncGenerator[bytes, None] so users (and linters) know aclose exists. small change but will be breaking for some duck-typed code? probably fine.

elaine: also check uvloop vs builtin loop differences; some of the CLOSE_WAIT behavior we've seen before correlated with uvloop's socket handling when tasks are cancelled without explicit close. add test matrix.

sam: I'll open a draft PR that: 1) introduces a StreamWrapper with aclose impl, 2) updates return types, 3) adds a unit test that cancels mid-iteration and asserts resp.closed and connection count returns.

matt: assign to me for review, please include repro script and CI flakiness notes. thanks. :pray:

sam: added PR link in thread (WIP) and attached small repro script. will ping when ready for review.

elaine: thanks — also add a note in the sample-app README about explicit cancellation patterns until SDK is patched. short workaround snippet there helps users.

sam: ack, will do.

matt: happy to pair if you want to tackle the wrapper impl tomorrow.

sam: thanks — appreciate it.
